Change c0462. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VI; 1831 Ch. XXIII.

Context before (unchanged): Nothing is so painful to the human mind as a great and sudden change.

1818 text: The sun might shine, or the clouds might lour; but nothing could appear to me as it had done the day before.

1831 text: The sun might shine, or the clouds might lower: but nothing could appear to me as it had done the day before.

Diff: The sun might shine, or the clouds might [-lour;-] {+lower:+} but nothing could appear to me as it had done the day before.

Context after (unchanged): A fiend had snatched from me every hope of future happiness: no creature had ever been so miserable as I was; so frightful an event is single in the history of man.

result.rationale: "lour" becomes "lower" (archaic/variant spelling of the verb meaning to scowl or darken); the sense of gloomy clouds is unchanged. The semicolon-to-colon shift is punctuation only.
